title: SLO-driven Terraform module for OTLP/Prometheus/Grafana + log-shipping with automated safe upgrades
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provisions a VPC-friendly observability stack (Prometheus + Grafana, OpenTelemetry Collector as OTLP forwarder, and log shipping agents). The module must include opinionated defaults for private deployments, built-in health checks and a safe, automated upgrade path driven by SLO verification. It should support deployment in Redwood Private (VPC) environments, including configuration for private endpoint networking, KMS-encrypted secrets, and optional operator-based lifecycle for low-touch upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Module provisions Prometheus (scrape + remote_write) and Grafana with declarative provisioning files via Terraform outputs
OTel Collector deployed as a scalable deployment or operator (configurable) exposing OTLP gRPC/HTTP endpoints inside the VPC
Log shipping implemented via Vector or Fluent Bit in a configurable mode (sidecar, DaemonSet, or standalone) with push to S3 or internal log router
Health checks: readiness/liveness, custom /health endpoints, and Prometheus alerts preconfigured for key failure modes
Automated upgrade pipeline: canary rollout, synthetic traffic validation, SLO checks (error rate/ingest latency), and automatic rollback on violation
Module supports KMS key id for secret encryption and IAM role boundaries for least-privilege access
Documentation and runbooks included in module README with upgrade playbook, rollback steps, and required terraform variables
Integration test (terragrunt variant) demonstrates create/upgrade/destroy flows in an isolated test VPC
tasks: Design module inputs/outputs and UX for private VPC: variables.tf sketch
Implement Prometheus helm chart wrapper with values for remote_write and serviceMonitor selectors
Implement Grafana provisioning via configmaps and Terraform-managed dashboards
Add OTEL Collector module with two deployment modes: "operator" and "deployment" and config templating
Add Vector/Fluent Bit module with routing to S3 or internal log router; RBAC and service account
Create healthcheck module: prometheusRules, synthetic probe job, kubernetes readiness checks
Build an upgrade orchestrator pattern: terraform plan detection -> canary apply -> synthetic tests -> SLO gating -> promote/rollback
Write docs, examples, and terragrunt test harness
Add CI pipeline that runs acceptance terragrunt tests and publishes a compatibility matrix
technical_notes: Prefer helm_release for Prometheus/Grafana for version pinning; expose values map with opinionated defaults
OTel config should be templated using jsonencode and allow hot-swap via configmap hash annotations to trigger rolling restarts
Use Kubernetes PodDisruptionBudget and minReadySeconds for safe upgrades
SLO gating implemented using a small test runner: synthetic traces/logs and query against Prometheus remote_read/Thanos to validate ingest latency < 500ms and error_rate < 0.5%
Upgrade path: apply to canary namespace (5% of collectors), run synthetic traffic for 10 minutes, evaluate SLOs, then roll to 100% if green
Module should expose a toggle 'upgrade_strategy' with options: manual | canary | operator_autoupdate
Secrets encrypted with KMS and passed as Kubernetes Secrets via External Secrets pattern if enabled
Provide hooks for pre-upgrade and post-upgrade scripts (e.g., migration jobs to reconcile dashboards or reindex alert rules)
decisions: Choose Vector as default log shipper (smaller footprint than Fluent Bit and richer transforms), with option to switch to Fluent Bit via variable
OTel operator mode added as opt-in to simplify lifecycle for customers who want reconciler semantics
SLO checks will run in CI and in-cluster 'prober' job during canary to avoid false positives from CI-only runs
Grafana will be provisioned with read-only dashboards by default and optional admin password rotation managed by the module
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Lee): request to add customer-visible toggle to disable Grafana provisioning for customers with self-managed dashboards
Security (Maya Kapoor): verify that KMS key policy prevents cross-account decrypt; require security_review_required for operator_autoupdate
SRE (Ethan Wang): suggested adding an observability-metered dashboard that shows canary vs baseline ingest latency during upgrades
